subject.title: fix: provider usage accounting, retry/overflow classification, and output clamping

question: Should empty thinking signatures remain an explicit public Anthropic compatibility option, or should support be confined to internally identified compatible backends?
rationale: The PR adds a public plugin SDK and model-config contract, and repository policy requires maintainer confirmation before choosing and permanently supporting that compatibility surface.

options.title: Complete the opt-in contract
options.body: Keep allowEmptySignature default-off and thread it through config validation, catalog normalization, documentation, and loaded-model tests.

options.title: Keep detection internal
options.body: Remove the public compatibility field and enable empty signatures only for narrowly identified backends with an established contract.

options.title: Separate this portion
options.body: Drop the empty-signature API from this PR and revisit it in a focused compatibility proposal while landing the independent provider fixes.

recommendation.title: Complete the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Keep allowEmptySignature default-off and thread it through config validation, catalog normalization, documentation, and loaded-model tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Anthropic provider work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the compatibility-surface choice.
